summary: The root مَسَسَ primarily means to touch, feel, or handle something with the hand. It can also imply affecting or reaching something, like an affliction or a blessing.

headwords.gloss: He made him; caused him, to touch the thing; he enabled him to touch it

parts.t: caused him, to touch the thing:
he enabled him to touch it.
He wetted the body with water;
caused water to wet the body.
He smeared his face with the perfume.
She smeared the sides of her cheeks with it;
He made a complaint to him.

headwords.def: إمسّهُ الشَّىْءَ He made him, or caused him, to touch the thing: (S, * IJ, M, A: *) he enabled him to touch it. (Mgh.) أَمَسَّ الجَسَدَ مَآءً , and الجَسَدَ بِمَآءٍ , (tropical:) He wetted the body with water; or caused water to wet the body. (Msb.) And أَمَسَّ وَجْهَهُ الطِّيبَ (tropical:) He smeared his face with the perfume. (Mgh.) And أَمَسَّتْهُ عَارِضَيْهَا , and بِعَارِضَيْهَا , (tropical:) She smeared the sides of her cheeks with it; namely, perfume. (Mgh.) أَمَسَّهُ شَكْوَى (tropical:) He made a complaint to him. (M, TA.)

headwords.def: تماسّا They (two bodies) touched each other; were, or became, in contact. (M, A, * K, *) Hence, (K,) (tropical:) They two came together in the way of مُبَاضَعَة : (S, Msb, * K: *) in this sense the verb is used in the Kur, lviii. 4 and 5. (S, TA.) See also مَسَّهَا .

headwords.gloss: Taste ye the first effect upon you of the fire of hell; the stroke thereof; the heat and pain thereof

parts.t: : see 1. It is used to denote [the first sensible effect of] anything annoying or hurtful that befalls a man. (TA.) Thus in the Kur, [liv. 48,] (TA,)
Taste ye the first effect upon you of the fire of hell:
of fever, before its taking him forcibly, and becoming apparent.
He did not feel the first sensation of fatigue.

headwords.def: مَسٌّ : see 1. It is used to denote [the first sensible effect of] anything annoying or hurtful that befalls a man. (TA.) Thus in the Kur, [liv. 48,] (TA,) ُوقُوا مَسَّ سَقَرَ (tropical:) Taste ye the first effect upon you of the fire of hell: (K, TA:) or the stroke thereof: (Jel:) or the heat and pain thereof. (Bd.) In like manner you say, (K,) وَجَدَ مَسَّ الحُمَّى (M, K) (tropical:) He felt the commencement, or first touch, [or access, ] of fever, before its taking him forcibly, and becoming apparent. (M, L.) And لَمْ يَجِدْ مَسًّا مِنَ النَّصَبِ (tropical:) He did not feel the first sensation of fatigue. (TA, from a trad.) headwords.gloss: in whom is a touch; stroke; of madness, insanity
headwords.def: مَمْسُوسٌ A man in whom is a touch, or stroke, ( مَسٌّ ,) of madness, insanity, or diabolical possession: (S, TA:) or mad, insane, or possessed by a devil. (AA, M, A, Mgh, K.)
